scenes.say: Your Docker container keeps exiting. What do you check first?

scenes.title: Logs and exit codes
scenes.say: First, check logs and exit codes. Use docker logs, docker ps dash a, and docker inspect for details.

scenes.label: exec
scenes.sub: Get a shell inside with docker exec -it web sh
scenes.say: If you need to poke around, open a shell inside with docker exec dash i t web sh.
Exit codes tell the story. One thirty seven means killed, usually by running out of memory. One is an app error. Zero means the main process finished cleanly.

scenes.question: What does exit 137 usually mean?
scenes.wrong: The app crashed due to a bug.
scenes.right: It was killed, often by running out of memory.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: What does exit one thirty seven usually mean? It's not just a bug. It's usually killed by running out of memory.
